title: Senior-wish verdict on HANDOFF.md letter
desc: Tool judges whether senior-wish paragraphs answered; exit 0 pass, 1 refused, 2 harness fault.
steps: WHAT THE TOOL IS

wkwish.cmd is the senior-wish verdict decider for HANDOFF.md. Reads previous letter from git history before session start, extracts paragraphs naming source files, checks if answered in current manifest. Exit codes: 0 = all wish paragraphs answered (proceed); 1 = refused with senior paragraph quoted verbatim; 2 = harness fault, cannot evaluate, NOT A PASS.
EXIT CODE 2 IS NOT A PASS
Unevaluated verdict clears nothing. Treating exit 2 as success reintroduces fail-open this gate prevents. Harness blocks letter commits on exit 2.

WISH FORMULA: EXISTENCE-FILTERED NOT MANIFEST-SUBTRACTED. AND THE ROW VERIFIER GREPS THE FUNCTION COLUMN AGAINST THE FILE -- measured 2026-09-03 by calling wk_manifest_row_is_verified twice: a real row returned TRUE, the identical row with a function name no file defines returned FALSE. Both calls were needed, since a predicate answering TRUE to everything is indistinguishable from a correct one on the positive case alone. Source .githooks/lib/manifest-row-verify.sh and check a row BEFORE pasting it into the letter; the refusal says the row is UNVERIFIED, which is a claim about evidence rather than about spelling

Wishes are PARAGRAPHS not files. Each paragraph naming sources is one row. NOT manifest-minus-previous. Instead: each source in prior paragraph checked if answered (exists in manifest without <FILL:>). ALL sources in row must pass.
PARAGRAPH-AS-ROW SHAPE
Each paragraph one row. Refusal quotes senior verbatim. Each unanswered source gets status. Skeleton MANIFEST row printed.
GATE SEAM
Gate in .githooks/lib/handoff-manifest-gate.sh main() after row scan before exit. Scoped to HANDOFF.md commits.
MEASURED NUMBERS
Current: 77 paragraphs total, 17 name sources, 15 unanswered, exit 1.

ONE WISH PER REFUSAL, and the length is the progress bar. WHEN: reading a wkwish or commit-gate refusal, or considering raising the cap. HOW: the refusal prints step (a) verbatim once, then ONE unanswered paragraph with its sources and its skeleton row, then a single line naming how many remain -- close that one, run wkwish again, get the next. WHY: measured 2026-08-31, it printed all fifteen with a skeleton row each, 269 lines, and the owner's reaction to reading it was that a reader skims a dump. At 36 lines it is read. Raise the cap only if you can say what a reader does with the extra ones. TWO THINGS STILL OWED HERE, both named by the owner the same day: the refusal should carry a SECOND paragraph for a step other than (a), since every skeleton row today is labelled (a) and steps (b) onward are never performed; and the step-text extraction still greps the literal '(a) DISPATCH' with a hardcoded sentence as fallback, so renaming that step in the skill would silently substitute a sentence nobody verified -- the same disease as a Stop hook reporting nine canonical steps while the skill documented thirteen. Extract by LABEL and let an unreadable skill say so.

NO LETTER, NO VERDICT, and INSTALL A CALLER NEVER A COPY. WHEN: running wkwish outside the repo, reading any refusal count, or installing this tool anywhere. HOW: the decider checks the letter path FIRST and returns 2 naming it; treat 2 as a harness fault that cleared nothing, never a refusal and never a pass. The installed entry in the shared bin is a two-line caller that runs the harness's own file by absolute path -- there is no copy of the decider or of session-init.sh beside it. WHY, both measured 2026-08-31: pointed at a nonexistent path it printed 17 senior wish paragraphs, 15 unanswered and refused, because the wish set comes from the PREVIOUS letter in git history while the answers come from the CURRENT letter's manifest, so a missing current letter makes every wish read as unanswered and the absence becomes the loudest possible refusal. And the earlier install shipped a COPY, which then needed a copy of its dependency beside it: the harness original ran 6.4s and the installed copy 81s, 13x, because from that folder every path it resolved was the wrong one and it did the work twice. Copies drift and copies lie about cost.

THE SKELETON CARRIES ITS HEADER, and the first column is WIRED. WHEN: reading a refusal, or changing what the skeleton prints. HOW: run wkwish and read the three lines it emits together -- the header, the separator, then the row; the columns are step, wired, function, skill, quote. WHY: measured 2026-08-31, it printed five pipe-separated values with no header and the owner said the field names have to be visible or the row means nothing. The first column is named WIRED rather than filename on purpose: the question it asks is where the thing is wired, not what file it lives in. NEXT STEP STILL OWED, and the rule matters more than the code: the second block must pick the descent step with the FEWEST manifest rows, never the first with ZERO. The zero rule goes silent once every label has one row, which is exactly what happened -- every skeleton said (a), readers filled (a), and steps (b) onward were never performed. Fewest-rows always names a step and names the least-served one, so the choice keeps moving as work lands. Derive the label list from the skill, never a hardcoded array.

VERIFIED: the descent LABEL SET is disputed by three sources at once, so any gate that derives labels must say WHICH source it read. WHEN: writing or reviewing anything that enumerates descent steps -- a skeleton row label, a per-step evidence check, a Stop-hook step count, or a manifest audit. HOW: take the labels from the ONE step of the descent skill that carries the order, the step whose text contains the (a) DISPATCH sentence -- run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff-howto and scan that step alone, never the whole output; then run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff for the law the procedure serves, since the core wins where the two disagree. WHY: measured 2026-08-31 in wkappbot-kih, three counts from three places. Scanning the DESCENT-ORDER STEP for a parenthesised short label yields TWELVE in order: a, a2, b, c, d, e, e2, f, g, h, h2, i. Scanning the WHOLE skill output yields THIRTEEN, the extra being (j) -- and THE CLAIM THAT USED TO STAND HERE, that (j) occurs only inside ordinary prose and is not a descent step at all, IS FALSE. Measured 2026-09-07: the skill states verbatim that THE OWNER FOUR CLOSING QUESTIONS become MANDATORY descent step (j), asked and ANSWERED IN WRITING before any session claims it has descended, so THIRTEEN is the correct count and a manifest without a (j) row is genuinely incomplete. Verify before trusting either number: grep the skill for the phrase descent step (j). The old wording was worse than a stale note because it taught a reader to treat a CORRECT refusal as a bug, and a session acting on it silently drops an owner-mandated step; I lost a commit round to exactly that. THE REAL ARTEFACT IS (s), NOT (j), and it does not come from prose either -- it comes from the READER OWN FOOTER, the line reading plus N DEV step(s) hidden, which is scanned only when the isolation grep has already failed because read-formatter elision truncated the descent-order step away from its marker. The global rules file meanwhile describes the descent as nine steps a to i. A sector implementing fewest-rows label selection scanned the whole output, duly selected (j), and printed a step text spliced out of unrelated paragraphs; the refusal looked authoritative and named a step that does not exist. THE COST IS ALREADY IN THE TREE: the current letter's manifest carries a (j) row, so a label nobody defined has already been written into a receipt. THE RULE: a label list is derived from one named passage or it is invented, and a gate that cannot say which passage it read is reporting a number rather than a fact -- the same disease as a Stop hook announcing nine canonical steps while the skill documented thirteen.

NAVIGATION: procedures live in the sibling, this core holds the contract. WHEN: you need to RUN the verdict, read a refusal block by block, or check what the tool still owes. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkwish-howto for the run commands including the sector-copy dependency override, the three-claims reading order, and the owed-work list; stay here for the exit-code contract and the wish formula. WHY: created 2026-08-31 because this core had grown past ten steps with no sibling tier at all, which scores it zero on the tier formula -- and a zero-scoring skill seals every study-lock that names it the moment one does. Splitting the procedure out is the fix the formula actually rewards, not trimming the contract.

TODO: the verdict must DIFF the predecessor's letter against the CURRENT one -- a wish paragraph WIRED AND THEN DELETED counts as COMPLETED and is worth one extra point, while a paragraph DELETED WITHOUT the wiring is a PENALTY that BLOCKS the commit (owner's design, recorded 2026-09-03 before it is built so nobody re-derives it). WHEN: you are reading this tool's score, wondering why removing a finished paragraph changed nothing, or about to implement either half. HOW: run 'wkappbot skill read wkwish-howto' for how to run the verdict and read its blocks, then verify the three facts this contract rests on before touching code -- paragraphs come ONLY from git show prev_commit HANDOFF.md at handoff-wish-verdict.sh line 129; the CURRENT letter is read at lines 137-143 but ONLY to extract the manifest table; and the work floor already exists as TEN INSERTED LINES per source this session under the comment WORK COUNTS NOT TYPING, so reuse that floor as the wiring evidence rather than inventing a second one. WHY: as of 2026-09-03 nothing anywhere compares the two letters, so deleting a paragraph moves the score by exactly zero in either direction -- measured by reading the live code rather than inferred -- and the contract had never been written into this skill or its siblings, so this was never an implementer's oversight but an unwritten requirement. The penalty half is what closes the obvious trap: crediting deletion would make emptying the list the cheapest route to a passing score, so the credit REQUIRES wiring evidence and an unwired deletion must refuse; and when matching a paragraph across the two letters prefer a FALSE PRESENT to a FALSE DELETED, because a missed point costs one session while a wrongly granted point costs the gate its meaning.

RESULT: SHIPPED 2026-09-03 in .githooks/lib/wish-deleted-credit.sh commit 3a21b3247 -- the rewrite branch now prints a banner, the count, the FIRST VANISHED PARAGRAPH VERBATIM and the git command that recovers the rest, while still returning rc 0 so a normal rewrite is never refused. Verified by exercising the branch itself, not by the module self-test which covers only the verdict function: rewrite 3-of-4 banners with stdout 0 0 and rc 0, no-deletion stays byte-for-byte silent, a real erasure still refuses with rc 1. The verdict ALREADY HOLDS the predecessor's letter, so a deleted wish paragraph must be printed LOUDLY and warned about, never skipped in one quiet line -- owner ruling 2026-09-03. WHEN: the output reads 'letter REWRITTEN (N of M wish paragraphs absent) -- deletion credit and erasure penalty both skipped', or you are implementing the rewrite branch. HOW: run wkappbot skill read letter-edit for the sibling gate's rule order and wkappbot skill read wkwish-howto for how to read each block, then make the absent case NOISY BEFORE the credit-versus-penalty question is settled -- print each vanished paragraph VERBATIM out of the previous letter the verdict already reads at handoff-wish-verdict.sh line 129, name the commit it disappeared in, and warn. The owner's words: the wish tool knows the predecessor's letter, so it must show the removed content very loudly and warn. WHY: the current behaviour is the worst of the three options. It detects the deletion, holds the exact text, and then says nothing a reader can act on, so an unrecorded removal and a completed-then-tidied one produce the identical single line and the session that did the removing gets no signal. Measured the same day in personal-docs: HANDOFF.md was overwritten wholesale, three of the senior's wish paragraphs went with it, and the only trace was that one skipped line, which did not read as an accusation and so was not treated as one. THE PRINCIPLE BEYOND THIS TOOL: a check that KNOWS what was destroyed and stays quiet is not neutral, it launders the destruction -- silence in the presence of evidence reads to every future session as permission. Step 18's credit-and-penalty design remains the eventual fix; this half must not wait for it, because printing what you already hold costs nothing.

INCIDENT: REWRITING the letter DELETES the manifest, which un-answers every wish the predecessor had closed, and the ratchet then blames you for not improving. WHEN: any descent where you overwrite HANDOFF.md rather than appending to it, which is the normal practice here and therefore the normal way to trigger this. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff for the letter contract, then APPEND your manifest rows and CARRY THE PREDECESSOR ROWS FORWARD under their own heading; before committing, run the repo-root verdict tool and compare the granted count against the previous letter's, because a granted count that FELL is proof you erased a record rather than proof you did nothing. WHY: measured 2026-09-03. My predecessor's manifest carried 32 rows and their letter stood at 6 granted. I rewrote the file, kept only my own rows, and granted went to ZERO -- the verdict reads answers ONLY from the CURRENT manifest, so a rewrite makes every prior answer vanish while the work itself sits untouched in the repo. wish-score-ratchet then refused two letter commits in a row with was 0 granted, now 0, and the message points at effort when the cause is deletion. THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS EXPENSIVE: the rows cost the predecessor a whole session to earn and cost me one paste to restore, but nothing in the tooling told me they were gone -- the count simply read zero, which is exactly what a session that had done nothing would also see. THE RULE: rewriting the letter is normal, dropping the manifest is not. A manifest row is a receipt for work that still exists, not a claim about who typed it, so carry the inherited rows and label them inherited.

DECISION: when this verdict shows a senior's own words, the WORDS COME FIRST and the tool's reasoning goes LAST -- owner ruling 2026-09-03, given three times, each narrowing the last. WHEN: writing or reviewing any output here that surfaces text a predecessor wrote, and the moment you catch yourself framing it with a banner, an equals-sign box or an imperative checklist. HOW: run wkappbot skill read letter-edit for the sibling gate's rule order and wkappbot skill read wkwish-howto for how the blocks are meant to read, then shape it as a LETTER -- one salutation naming the reader and the act, the predecessor paragraphs verbatim and unbroken, then the count, the recovery command, the signature and any withheld score at the bottom. WHY: measured in .githooks/lib/wish-deleted-credit.sh the day a session deleted three senior wish paragraphs and filed a complete descent receipt over the hole. THREE CORRECTIONS IN SEQUENCE. First, the banner emphasised the tool's own scolding, which the owner said only flatters the tool while the senior's text stays hidden. Second, equals-sign frames and imperative lists read as SYSTEM MESSAGE, and he named the consequence exactly: Sonnet starts probing the frame and Haiku analyses it instead of the content. Third, I argued to keep one framing line ABOVE the text because the deleted material held a stale OPEN item that reads as a live instruction -- he overruled it and answered better, make the top line a SALUTATION, since a letter frames itself and a reader knows on sight that it is a person's past words. Then tightened once more: a bare Dear junior is polite enough to skim past, so the line must name the reader AND the act, because a model can auto-dismiss a notice but cannot auto-dismiss being addressed and accused in one sentence. THE RULE BEHIND ALL THREE: why the tool did this can be worked out slowly, but the senior's wish has to land reflexively. FOURTH, 2026-09-03: the rebuke ROTATES across six variants, because a fixed opening line is learned after a few exposures and skimmed, while a line that changes each run has to be read to be understood -- every variant still does the same two jobs, name the reader and name the act. AND NO PROFANITY, asked and declined the same minute: this output rides git hooks into CI logs and other AI families' transcripts, where swearing is permanent, can trip a content filter and silently truncate the whole message, and reads as emotion -- which is the easiest thing of all to dismiss. The sting comes from specificity, since you deleted my words lands harder than any insult.

VERIFIED: the previous letter this verdict scores against is chosen by TIMESTAMP, not by position, and the revision a session naturally reaches for is a different one. WHEN: you are about to recover manifest rows or wish paragraphs out of git history because the verdict says they are unanswered, or you are wondering why work you landed moved the granted count by zero. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkwish-howto for how to read the refusal blocks, then resolve the revision FIRST with 'git log -n 1 --before=<session start UTC> --format=%H -- HANDOFF.md' and recover only from what that prints -- the selector is at handoff-wish-verdict.sh line 128 and the letter is read at line 137. WHY: measured 2026-09-03 in wkappbot-kih. For a session beginning 02:59Z the selector returned be9e919d7, while the revision carrying the MOST manifest rows -- and the one that looked like the obvious predecessor from git log -- was 8d632bed7. Rows recovered from the wrong revision answer paragraphs this verdict never reads, so the work lands, the count stays put, and the output is indistinguishable from a session that did nothing. The failure is silent in both directions: nothing errors, and the ratchet then reports lack of effort for work that was actually done against the wrong target.

INCIDENT: the erasure detector has a false-positive floor and the remedy line it prints is destructive. WHEN: wkwish ends with No score this run plus a banner saying N more of my paragraphs are gone. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff-howto before touching the letter, and measure the real deletion with git log --oneline -3 -- HANDOFF.md followed by git diff PREV HEAD -- HANDOFF.md piped to grep -c for removed lines. WHY: measured 2026-09-06, driving wk_wish_deleted_apply with prev equal to cur, byte-identical at 58992 chars, still reported 12 erased paragraphs, and an independent awk reimplementation of the same longest-line-key plus grep -qF rule reported 12 too, so the floor is in the rule not one implementation; the printed remedy git checkout HEAD~1 -- HANDOFF.md was a no-op that day because HEAD~1 HANDOFF.md was byte-identical to HEAD, and it becomes a letter-destroying revert whenever the newest letter is the HEAD commit; the only real deletion in that letter history was 73 lines, all pipe-prefixed manifest rows preserved in the committed sidecar HANDOFF-manifest-20260906.md, zero prose lines, and the detector does not even count pipe rows.

INCIDENT: wkwish accused a session of erasing 134 senior paragraphs when the true number was TWO, and both of those are accounted for -- measured 2026-09-06 in personal-docs, far past the false-positive floor step 23 already records. WHEN: wkwish ends with 'No score this run' plus 'N more of my paragraphs are gone', and especially when it ALSO prints 'this run could not name the predecessor commit'. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff-howto before touching the letter, then resolve the predecessor yourself with git log -n 1 --before=<session start UTC> --format=%H -- HANDOFF.md (it returned 8125813f here while the tool claimed it could not name one) and replicate the detector's own rule -- for each paragraph of git show PREV:HANDOFF.md take its LONGEST line as the key and test whether that key still occurs anywhere in the current HANDOFF.md, repeating across every plausible predecessor revision rather than one. WHY: the arithmetic settles it without trusting either side. The current letter was 2523 lines against the predecessor's 954; git diff PREV showed 43 removed lines total, 8 of them manifest pipe rows and 35 prose; and a paragraph cannot vanish without at least one removed line, so 134 erased paragraphs is impossible on its face. The key-absence replication returned 2 against the correct predecessor and 1, 5, 3, 4 against the four next-older revisions, so no revision choice comes near the accusation. The two real absences were a HEADING retitled in place -- '## DONE - this session' became a dated Korean heading whose own note says the body was untouched, done to escape the handoff-names gate -- and one ledger paragraph deliberately closed with a recorded triplet per senior-letter-constitution step 6. Neither is a deletion. THE TRAP THIS CLOSES: the printed remedy invites a revert, and reverting here would have destroyed a 1613-line letter to restore two paragraphs that were never lost, so the accusation is more dangerous than the thing it accuses. TWO FURTHER DEFECTS in the same run: the tool printed 'could not name the predecessor commit' while the documented command resolves it fine, and the run ended with 'handoff-wish-verdict.sh: line 399: rt: command not found' on a 398-line file -- the signature of a STALE exported function shadowing the on-disk one, since the wish libs end in export -f and wk_wish_deleted_noscore had gained a second prev-commit parameter that same day, so an older one-argument copy inherited from the environment would both ignore that argument and report line numbers past the end of the current file.

VERIFIED: two of the three defects in step 24 are already dead, and my stale-exported-function explanation for them was WRONG -- corrected here rather than left standing, because a wrong root cause in a skill is worse than none. WHEN: you are reading step 24, or you hit the 'could not name the predecessor commit' line or an 'rt: command not found' at line 399. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-do-not-read-it rule, then re-run the decider yourself from the repo root before believing any of step 24's secondary claims -- bash .githooks/lib/handoff-wish-verdict.sh in the repo whose letter you are grading. WHY, measured 2026-09-06 immediately after step 24 was written. THE STALE-EXPORT THEORY IS FALSIFIED: wish-deleted-credit.sh contains no export -f at all (only handoff-wish-verdict.sh line 397 does, for its own entry point), and env showed ZERO BASH_FUNC_ entries, so nothing was shadowing anything. THE REAL CAUSE WAS A SIX-MINUTE-OLD WIRING GAP: diff against .bak/handoff-wish-verdict.sh.bak-20260906-132021 shows line 314 read wk_wish_deleted_noscore $quiet with no second argument, and the 8th prev_commit parameter had landed in the credit module between the 13:14 and 13:18 backups -- so the caller simply was not passing it yet. Both are fixed on disk and my live re-run printed the resolved commit correctly and produced no 'rt' line at all. WHAT SURVIVES FROM STEP 24 IS THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS: the 134-paragraph accusation reproduces exactly on the current code. LOCALISATION SO FAR, so the next session does not redo it: wk_wish_deleted_verdict is CORRECT in isolation -- source the module, hand it a paragraph that is present and the real letter text, and it answers PRESENT, while a fabricated paragraph answers ERASED. wk_wish_deleted_apply is ALSO correct when called by hand with a real cur_letter -- forced into its rewrite branch with the first twelve lines of the predecessor letter it answered 'That was all 0 of them', for the very paragraphs the live run prints as gone. So the fault is not the matching rule; it is in what the HOST passes as current_letter_text, and the count 142 of 167 is the exact signature of that argument arriving EMPTY, since every paragraph with a key of 24 or more characters that is not a manifest pipe row then reads as absent.

RESULT: the wish decider's predicate is EDITED-THIS-SESSION, not WIRED, and that single fact explains every shape of the letter deadlock recorded across 08-31, 09-02 and 09-06. WHEN: letter-edit refuses HANDOFF.md with 'N of M wired' and you are about to go looking for a missing call site. HOW: run 'wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff' step 28 first -- run the decider, do not guess -- then read Test-WkWishGate.ps1 lines 50 to 53 in wkappbot-kih/tools/wkharness-common-wishgate/. It builds a HashSet of BASENAMES from $ChangedPaths and marks a wish unwired when its basename is absent from that set; the cache it feeds is .tmp/wkharness/wish-counts.txt, two comma-separated integers. So the count moves when you TOUCH a file and never when you WIRE. RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-09-07 AND THIS STEP HELD, against a contradicting authority that looked more current than it. The Stop hook changed its own wording that day to assert A WISH CLOSES ON A MANIFEST ROW -- file, function, skill, quote -- and A COMMIT IS ONLY ITS FIRST COLUMN, so wiring alone moves this number by ZERO. That is FALSE about this decider: reading the function again end to end, the wishes are BASENAMES scraped by regex from the PREVIOUS letter under OPEN or NEXT headings, changed is a HashSet of basenames taken from ChangedPaths, and unwired is simply the wishes absent from it -- there is no manifest, no row, no column and no commit anywhere in the predicate. I nearly retracted this step on the hook text alone, having already told the owner several times that the counter was a miscount, then reversed myself again when the hook contradicted me; the source settled it in one read. TWO RULES. FIRST, A GUARD MESSAGE IS A SURFACE AND SURFACES GO STALE OR WRONG JUST LIKE SKILLS -- when a hook and a measured skill step disagree, the CODE is the tiebreaker, and it is usually twenty lines away. SECOND, MY OWN OBSERVATION DID NOT DISCRIMINATE and I should have noticed sooner: committing a touched file left the number frozen, which is equally consistent with both stories, because the file was not one of the senior wish basenames at all. When an observation fits both hypotheses it is not evidence -- go and read the predicate one. MEASURED 2026-09-06: all eight named files had real callers -- ElideRankedWholeUnits at ReadFormatter.cs:310 and EyeCmdPipeClient.TryDelegate at Program.Main.cs:280 were hand-verified -- and the counter still read 1 of 9; it advanced to 2 of 9 the moment SkillCommand.Helpers.cs was edited for a completely unrelated bug fix. THE TRAP, and it is the reason this needs writing down: the remedy the gate suggests, dispatch parallel sectors, CANNOT clear it when the sectors are read-only measurement work, because a sector that changes nothing changes no path. A session that wants the letter open is therefore steered toward editing seven healthy files it has no business touching -- which satisfies the gate and fails its purpose, the same shape as a bare-number --like or a WKHARNESS_AGENT_MODEL spoof. DO NOT PAY IT THAT WAY. This also fails the owner's own test for a guard bug (opus-self-reflection): it blocks on state the session's will did not create. THE FIX BELONGS IN THE DECIDER -- compare against call sites, or rename the count to say what it measures. CORRECTION 2026-09-06 to claude-session-handoff step 36, measured against it directly: the trigger is NOT 'the edit introduces a source filename'. That step records such an edit as PASSING and it is wrong. THREE attempts in one session, same file, same anchor: one naming eight source files, one naming three, and one naming ZERO -- referring to everything by skill id and prose instead -- and ALL THREE were refused with the BYTE-IDENTICAL message and the same debug line, 2 of 9 wired, listing the same seven basenames. The count never moved because nothing in the working tree changed between them. So the predicate is the ChangedPaths basename set and NOTHING ELSE: content is never examined, and no amount of rewriting can satisfy a check that does not read what you wrote. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE is the reason this is written down -- a successor who believes step 36 will spend attempts rewording the letter, which is exactly the behaviour this gate cluster keeps producing and exactly what a gate must never teach. Stop after ONE refusal and spend the time on code. AND THE GENERAL RULE: when a gate refuses twice with a byte-identical message, that identity IS the evidence -- a check that varied with your input would have varied its complaint. THE RING HAS A THIRD GATE AND COMPACTION MAKES IT UNSATISFIABLE -- measured 2026-09-06, and this is the part that ends a descent rather than merely delaying it. Order of refusals on one letter: wish-gate refuses the EDIT (use wkappbot file edit, the sanctioned ROOT path, which passes); handoff-names then refuses the COMMIT until every landed file and edited skill is named, which is fair and satisfiable; and manifest-gate then demands a five-field row for EVERY descent step, each row's filename verified against THIS SESSION'S commit log. THAT LAST CHECK IS THE WALL: compaction moves the session start marker PAST the session's own earlier commits, so files genuinely landed hours ago -- verified by git show --stat, sitting in the log with their hashes -- are invisible to it, and a truthful row is refused as unbacked. Twelve steps therefore need twelve rows nobody can honestly fill. DO NOT FILL THEM ANYWAY. The gate's own text says a row you cannot fill truthfully is work you have not finished, do not invent the row -- so repeating one committed filename across twelve rows satisfies the mechanism and betrays the purpose, which is the same shape as a bare-number --like. THE SANCTIONED END STATE IS PRINTED BY THE GATE ITSELF: not descending, then do not commit this file, leave the letter in the working tree. So a complete letter left UNCOMMITTED is a correct outcome and not a failure -- say so plainly rather than grinding. PROTECT IT THE ONLY WAY THAT WORKS: put every finding into SKILLS as you go, because those commit freely and sync to HQ, and the letter then carries no knowledge that would die with it. Check what survives by reading a skill, never by reading the letter. UNTIL THEN, take the exit claude-session-handoff steps 36 and 37 already name: leave the letter complete on disk and report through the channel still open.
author: claude
